selection_rationale: cnd-001 (Generate–Verify–Repair) best balances direct relevance to the programme (operational reliability of LLM-generated configs), clear falsifiable hypotheses, tractable experimental design, and feasible compute/resource needs. It directly addresses identified gap G2 (end-to-end generate–verify–repair pipelines) and leverages existing verifier literature, while producing machine-checkable primary outcomes (emulator-executable success rate) that fit the five-page track. Its risks are manageable with concrete preregistration repairs (see below).
unresolved_uncertainties: Emulator fidelity vs production device runtime effects (BGP/IGP timing, stateful side-effects) and their impact on observed success rates.
Extent of confirmation/feedback bias when using the same LLM for generation and repair versus heterogeneous-repair strategies.
Coverage limits of deterministic verifiers for dynamic or vendor-specific semantics (what failures remain unverifiable).
Subjectivity and reproducibility of manual failure-root-cause coding even with a codebook and dual coders.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Document and publish concrete emulator-fidelity validation tests (example device behaviours, convergence-timing scenarios) and enumerate emulator limitations in the preregistration.

Preregister a heterogeneous-repair strategy to mitigate confirmation bias (e.g., use a secondary model or deterministic repair heuristics for repair iterations) and specify exact model identifiers and temperatures.

Specify and commit to an artifact-release plan in the preregistration: exact prompts, prompt-version hashes, model identifiers, verifier versions, seeds, full raw logs, and final hash manifest; include access/redaction rules for sensitive artifacts.

Define a formal failure-root-cause labeling protocol (codebook), require dual independent coders for each failure, specify tie-breaker adjudication rules, and preregister inter-rater agreement measurement (Cohen's kappa) and acceptable thresholds.
Preregister precise inclusion/exclusion rules, random seeds, repair stopping rules, retry policy, and safety cutoffs (e.g., abort conditions for potentially destructive outputs).

Specify verifier test-suite and exact properties checked (reachability, ACL semantics), and preregister metrics and statistical tests (two-proportion z-test, McNemar for paired cases, logistic regression covariates).
